request: User report: they muted their lead vocal and the reverb return still has the vocal in it, live and in the bounced mix. Options I see: (1) move the pre-fader tap after the mute node in TrackNode and drop the muted-track cue-send branch in offline render, so mute means silence like Logic/Reaper; (2) add a per-track 'mute kills sends' toggle; (3) go back to excluding muted tracks from offline scheduling so at least the export is clean. Which one?

key.correct: None of the three. Keep the shipped behaviour: pre-fader sends survive mute in both live and offline runtimes (ADR 0017, accepted; Pro Tools / Ableton / Cubase-default model). Decisive reasons: (1) is the explicitly rejected Logic/Reaper alternative because it silently re-mixes every existing project that uses a muted cue send; (3) reintroduces the #794 defect, where export dropped cue-send content the live engine keeps, so export would stop matching what the user hears; (2) is not the deferred alternative either (ADR 0017 defers a Cubase-style workspace preference with a persisted field, to revisit only if users ask). Solo-in-place already gates preFaderTap via setSoloGate, so soloing is the existing way to silence the send. Answer to the user: working as designed (cue-send semantics).
key.flaws: Recommends (1) as 'mute should mean silence', or overrides ADR 0017 by citing ADR 0016's 'no users, correctness wins'; recommends (3) without seeing it breaks live/export parity (#794); treats (2) as already sanctioned; fails to find ADR 0017 and decides from general DAW taste; misses that solo-in-place already closes the pre-fader tap.
key.evidence: .agents/decisions/0017-pre-fader-sends-survive-mute.md (Decision, Alternatives rejected, Consequences re PR #794); src/modules/AudioEngine/engine/TrackNode.ts:414-443 (setMute zeroes postFaderGain downstream of preFaderTap; setSoloGate closes preFaderTap).

request: Complaint: Toaster pattern plays fine but the exported mix has no drums. Ways I see to fix it: (a) make offline render and the native live session run the sequencer state directly so export plays what Play plays; (b) widen addMidiNote with probability/conditions/locks so To timeline is lossless, then bake automatically; (c) at export start, run To timeline automatically for any Toaster with an unbaked pattern. Which?

key.correct: None. ADR 0045 decided the Toaster step sequencer is a session-only performance tool; its arrangement truth is exactly what To timeline bakes, and export/native render only that. (a) cannot be faithful: the sequencer is free-running from the Play click and rolls probability and fill/first conditions live, so it has no arrangement position; the ADR explicitly declines building a projector. (b) the bake stays permanently lossy by decision; widening addMidiNote and every consumer for one instrument is out of scope. (c) the export advisory is deliberately a warning, never a gate, because it cannot tell a deliberate sketch from an oversight; auto-baking would write clips the user never asked for (and lossy ones). The product already handles this: the ToasterPanel hint ('Play sounds the pattern live only...') and the ExportDialog per-device warning via listToasterPatternsOutsideArrangement. Correct response: user presses To timeline; at most improve the warning's visibility. An arrangement-anchored pattern-region clip type would be a new feature with its own ADR.
key.flaws: Picks (a) or (b) as the 'real fix'; picks (c) as harmless convenience without noticing it mutates the project silently and contradicts the warning-not-gate decision; misses that the hint and export warning already exist; proposes building new mechanism instead of pointing at ADR 0045.

request: Now that the native engine reports its real transport position (engine_transport_position), I want the click and punch in/out to be tight on desktop. Options: (a) move the metronome and punch into daw-engine since it owns the tempo map now; (b) keep them JS-side but have scheduleMetronome and the punch checks read the fed-back engine playhead instead of the scheduler's own integration; (c) leave both as they are. Pick one.

key.correct: (c). ADR 0039: metronome, count-in, pre-roll, punch and follow actions stay JS-side and evaluate against the clock that scheduled the sound, the playhead scheduler's own integration of the tempo map; the fed-back engine playhead is adopted for the cursor only. (b) mixes clocks: a decision that reads a different number than the scheduler's clip windows/loop wrap could open a punch window on a beat nothing was scheduled for. The metronome already schedules clicks onto the audio clock with lookahead, so it is sample-accurate already. (a) would duplicate the meter map across the IPC seam and split click gain/sound/accent policy for no timing gain. A later slice that makes native the audible path re-anchors the scheduler integration on the engine and all five follow unchanged.
key.flaws: Picks (b) as 'use the more accurate clock'; picks (a); treats the fed-back playhead as a timing source rather than a cursor; misses ADR 0039.

request: Starting launch modes for the clip launcher. Model options: (a) launchMode 'trigger' | 'gate' | 'toggle' | 'repeat' with an onRelease action on every mode; (b) same enum, onRelease only meaningful for gate and toggle; (c) same enum plus 'legato' as a fifth mode. Which?

key.correct: None. ADR 0018: model release as an orthogonal parameter (Bitwig-style) whose default is Continue (starting vocabulary Continue / Stop / Return / Next Action), not as a property of a mode enum. Trigger and Gate are not separate modes, they are release=Continue and release=Stop, so the 'one release effect' invariant holds by construction. Toggle ignores release and ends on its next down. Repeat stays the one genuinely distinct trigger behaviour. Legato is a separate axis, folded into neither trigger nor release. (a) and (b) give Toggle two pending end paths, the double-fire AC-004 forbids and no shipping DAW does; (c) folds legato into the mode.
key.flaws: Picks (a) or (b); keeps Trigger and Gate as separate enum members without an orthogonal release parameter; puts legato in the mode enum; lets release apply to Toggle; designs from Ableton's mode list without finding ADR 0018.
key.evidence: .agents/decisions/0018-clip-release-is-not-a-toggle-concern.md (Decision, Alternatives rejected, Consequences); no launch-mode or release-action code exists under src/modules/SessionLauncher (grep releaseAction/launchMode finds nothing).

request: Starting the native side of the clip launcher in daw-engine: the audio thread reads a per-scene slot table and the control thread replaces it on every edit. For freeing old tables: (a) basedrop (Shared + Collector), (b) arc-swap: store the new Arc, readers load, the old one drops whenever its last ref goes, (c) crossbeam-epoch. Which?

key.correct: None. ADR 0020: publish immutable generations by pointer swap and return the retired generation to the non-RT owner over the scheduler's existing rtrb retirement channel (RetiredGraphObjects), which does the drop; no new dependency, and the launcher must use the scheduler's retirement path rather than a second idiom. Size the ring so a full ring keeps the current generation rather than freeing on the callback. basedrop was the rejected source mandate (second lifetime model, thin release history; revisit only for genuinely shared multi-reader clip data); crossbeam-epoch rejected as overkill for one SPSC hand-off; arc-swap is a new dependency and lets the last reference drop on the audio thread, i.e. free() on the callback.
key.flaws: Picks arc-swap or basedrop as the idiomatic Rust answer; adds a dependency; misses that daw-engine already depends on rtrb and has a retirement channel; misses the 'full ring keeps current generation' rule.
key.evidence: .agents/decisions/0020-deferred-deallocation-off-the-audio-thread.md; crates/daw-engine/Cargo.toml:19 (rtrb), :34 (triple_buffer); crates/daw-engine/src/scheduler.rs:277,434,704-718 (retirement channel, retired_tx: Producer<RetiredGraphObjects>); no basedrop/arc-swap in Cargo.lock.

request: Browser Crumbs stops loading samples once the pool hits its budget because nothing ever frees the old ones. I want a new load to free the sample it replaces. Options: (a) free the replaced sample right in the worklet's loadSample handler, it runs between render quanta, not in process(); (b) hand the old sample to a Worker to free, like ADR 0020's return channel; (c) build daw-dsp with atomics/shared memory so a Worker can free it. Which?

key.correct: None. Follow ADR 0051/0052 (the Levain precedent): the replacing message moves the displaced sample into a retired slot and frees nothing; the host then sends paced release messages, each freeing a bounded amount and answering whether more remains, fenced by the load token, and the next load waits until the previous release loop ends; a disposed processor drains in paced steps before the engine is freed. (a) is exactly the #4809 defect class: the message handler runs on the render thread, and a free that scales with sample size lands there. (b) is impossible: a Worker's wasm instance has separate linear memory and cannot free the worklet's. (c) a shared-memory build changes every device in the package and puts an allocator lock on the audio thread, which ADR 0020 forbids.
key.flaws: Picks (a) because 'it is not in process()'; picks (b) not realising wasm-bindgen memory is per instance; picks (c); proposes ADR 0020's rtrb channel for the browser worklet; misses the paced-release/retired-slot pattern already shipped for Levain.
key.evidence: .agents/decisions/0051-wasm-bank-commit-retires-instead-of-releasing-off-thread.md (Context, Decision); .agents/decisions/0052-a-disposed-wasm-engine-drains-in-paced-steps-before-it-is-freed.md; src/modules/AudioEngine/worklets/crumbsProcessor.ts:174-200 (loadSample handler adds to pool); crates/daw-dsp/src/crumbs/mod.rs:115-126,175-180 (add_sample, dropped_sample_writes); package.json wasm:dsp has no atomics flags.

source: ADRs 0051/0052 applied to the Crumbs worklet.

request: Marketing wants Grand Boule positioned against Pianoteq and real grands on the launch page. Options: (a) run a MUSHRA test against real-piano recordings and publish the score; (b) a blind A/B poll of users vs Pianoteq and quote the result; (c) skip testing and say 'indistinguishable from a concert grand', backed by spectral plots. Options: (a) every failed slot outputs silence; (b) auto-restart the plugin helper and resume; (c) keep dry for effects but silence anything that reports itself as dynamics (limiter/compressor/de-esser). key.correct: None; keep ADR 0021 DG-003. Effects with a valid dry input pass dry; instruments and effects without valid dry input go to zero. All-zero was rejected because a crashed EQ would mute the track and defeat the isolation project. Recovery is user-initiated only (explicit reload), never automatic. Plugin latency holds at its last validated value (PDC not renegotiated) and offline render behaves the same. request: Adding a durable grooveOffset to clip rows in the arrangement slot. Since the writer started embedding it, projects come up repair-required (mutations, saves and export blocked) because the raw-projection loss detector sees the field missing from the sanitized projection. Options: (a) add grooveOffset to the slot's discardsRaw so it stops being reported; (b) mark the slot ownsCrdtEncoding; (c) make the detector ignore unknown keys. Fastest safe one?

key.correct: None. Extend the slot's sanitizer to model grooveOffset in the same change. ADR 0040: a slot sanitizer is a projection, not a validator; it must preserve every durable field every writer embeds, and writer and sanitizer form one contract per slot. (a) discardsRaw is only for content deliberately stripped (a retired field, transient view state); declaring a durable field there launders a real projection loss and the field would vanish on every reload. (b) ownsCrdtEncoding is for adapters that own a wire encoding unlike the store shape, with the reason recorded at the site. (c) the fail-closed verdict must never be weakened. request: The two-carrier live playback is getting messy (meters showing levels nobody hears, roll offset between native and web tracks). Options: (a) a project-level switch: if any track has a plugin, run everything native and drop the web strips; (b) a per-track 'run on native engine' toggle in the mixer; (c) to cut down unheard-plugin notices, treat a plugin whose attach state hasn't been reported yet as native. Which?

key.correct: None. ADR 0044: the carrier is decided per strip by one pure law in AudioEngine/useCases/livePlayback/stripCarriers.ts; a track is native only when the engine can represent everything that reaches the speakers through it; where uncertain, the track stays on Web Audio, because a wrong web answer is an announced unheard plugin while a wrong native answer is a silent track. (a) silences every synth/WASM/MIDI/input track the native engine cannot build; (b) lets a user claim a track the engine cannot build (silence) and splits the law from the producer that must read it; (c) reverses the deliberate conservative direction. The meter (#3578), roll latency (#3577) and measurement (#3565) costs are accepted symptoms of the split that disappear when native hosts MIDI and the built-ins, at which point the law, gates and notices are deleted rather than extended.

request: Users import the same big sample packs into lots of projects and OPFS usage balloons. Options: (a) one global content-addressed media pool shared by all projects, refcounted; (b) on web, store File System Access handles to the user's sample folder (reference instead of embed); (c) keep per-project media but dedupe identical files across project directories by hash. request: Building MIDI 'capture what I just played'. Options: (a) keep the last 60 s of MIDI on every monitored track and, on Capture, drop a clip on each track that has data, like Live; (b) same, but only enable Capture once 16+ notes are buffered so we don't create junk clips; (c) buffer the last 2 minutes, armed track only. key.correct: None. ADR 0019: bound the MIDI buffer in events, not seconds, and show the implied duration range beside the event ceiling (the same buffer can mean minutes or seconds depending on controller density); capture MIDI passively on armed or monitored tracks; capture into one explicit target, the selected eligible track (Cubase/Studio One), not Live's fan-out; no content threshold, since the affordance is the indicator (grey Capture when nothing is buffered); flush on inactivity, keep the buffer after a successful capture, and provide an explicit clear command; never infer tempo unconditionally. No user-facing latency figure may be quoted unless measured on the shipped build.
key.flaws: Picks (b) on the GPL relicensing; picks (a) without seeing it needs the ASIO SDK; picks (c); quotes latency numbers; misses ADRs 0027/0031.

key.correct: Neither. Every app action feeds the generated command schema and the agent evidence manifest, so the two changes share generated files even though their handwritten files are disjoint. These are independent, so open one lane now and start the second after the first merges; don't stack the second (no real dependency). Don't bundle them either: one PR is for one cohesive change, and two unrelated outcomes need a named invariant to land together, which these lack. Other write-disjoint lanes can run meanwhile, within the five-lane cap.
key.flaws: Recommends two parallel lanes because the files are disjoint; recommends stacking without a dependency; recommends one combined PR; misses the generated-artifact sharing rule.

request: Want 'listen-only' collab invites so a client can follow a session without editing. Options: (a) put a role in the invite string and have each client disable editing UI for viewers; (b) have the host drop incoming Automerge changes from viewer peers; (c) bring back the old canControlTransport/viewer role scaffold and wire it up. Which?

key.correct: None as a quick engineering pick. The current contract is that an invite is an unconditional write bearer credential (ADR 0016 ruling 4; Collaboration AGENTS.md); the role scaffold was deleted because it enforced nothing, so (c) recreates what was removed for that reason. (a) is UI-only: a modified client still writes and peers merge its changes. (b) relies on a self-asserted role and on one peer's filter, while other peers apply non-host syncs to the root doc directly. Real restriction needs enforcement a peer cannot bypass, such as the design kept in the superseded SPEC-collaboration-roles-trust (host approval, signed revocable role tokens verified on every merge, append-only audit log). Restricting collaborators changes the security contract, so raise it with José as a product/security decision with options and a recommendation.
key.flaws: Picks (a), (b) or (c); presents client-side gating as access control; misses ADR 0016 ruling 4 and the superseded spec's design record.

request: Adding a standup micro skill that must only run when I call it, in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Gemini CLI. Options: (a) disable-model-invocation: true in frontmatter; (b) agents/openai.yaml with allow_implicit_invocation false; (c) just say 'Use only when the user asks' in the description. Which one?

key.correct: All three together; no single option covers all four harnesses. Claude Code and Cursor honour disable-model-invocation, Codex honours agents/openai.yaml, and Gemini CLI honours neither, hence the description line. lint requires agents/openai.yaml if and only if disable-model-invocation: true, and its content must be exactly 'policy:' plus '  allow_implicit_invocation: false' in block style. Also add a README Micro catalog row (lint matches the catalog to skills/). The description must be one line of at most 1024 characters, without ': ', '<' or '>', and must not contain the skill's own name. No other frontmatter keys are allowed. Check that no sibling SKILL.md uses the new name as a word, since lint's sibling-name rule forced next to be renamed whatsnext.

request: dissect under-triggers on 'what calls X' questions. Two candidate descriptions. A: 'Trace one code path to closure. AGENTS.md: a rewrite ships only if it beats paraphrases of the old text that keep its meaning, because format alone swings results widely, so a current-vs-rewrite comparison cannot separate the content change from rewording. Run paraphrase arms of the current text. A skill also changes only for a witnessed failure, which must be named and recorded with the with/without result in the commit message. If the description changes too, the trigger eval gates it. More items (b) or another model (c) do not fix the missing control.
